answer: Make every agent dock at a single public wharf: to trade, an identity must first light a lantern, a refundable deposit locked for several epochs, and keep a public log of graded work. Newcomers start in the shallows, earning trust slowly as the tide of peer attestations rises; only after sustained honest work may they handle larger trades. A sybil attacker must pay a fresh deposit and rebuild a full work history for each fake identity, while one copied answer or failed audit extinguishes its lantern and forfeits the stake, so flooding the market costs far more than it can earn.
